clock_offset_readout_query: Read the time shown by the clock.
Start from the time shown on the clock.
Use the analog clock as the starting time.
Base the calculation on the clock face.
clock_time_order_label_query: Order the labeled clocks by the times shown. Within the 12-hour cycle, 12 o'clock comes before 1 o'clock.
Compare the four labeled clock times. Treat the 12-hour cycle as starting at 12, then 1, then later hours.
Use the labeled analog clocks and the answer cards. The ordering is earliest to latest in a single 12-hour cycle starting at 12.
Read each labeled clock, then choose the card whose label order runs from earliest to latest, with 12 before 1.
Sort the four clock labels by shown time in the same 12-hour cycle, where 12 is the start of the cycle.
clock_hand_angle_value_query: Use the two hands on the analog clock.
Compare the positions of the two clock hands.
Use the hour hand and minute hand shown on the clock.
Base the answer on the smaller angle formed by the two hands.
Read the hand positions on the clock face.
clock_full_time_readout_query: Use all three hands on the analog clock.
Read the hour, minute, and second hands.
Use the three visible hand positions on the clock face.
Base the time on the hour hand, minute hand, and second hand.
Read the complete analog clock display.
clock_alarm_wait_time_value_query: The dark hour and minute hands show the current time. The red alarm hand points to the alarm hour on the same 1-12 hour scale as the numerals; the alarm minute is :00.
Read the current time from the dark hands. The red alarm hand uses the clock's 1-12 hour scale to mark an alarm hour, with alarm minutes fixed at :00.
Use the dark hands for the current time. The red alarm hand is an hour-scale alarm pointer, so it marks an alarm time at that hour and :00 minutes.
The black/blue hands show the current time. The red alarm hand points at the alarm hour on the clock's hour scale, and the alarm minute is :00.
Treat the red alarm hand as a distinct hour-scale alarm pointer. It marks an alarm time at the indicated hour and :00 minutes.

minutes_after: What time will it be {delta_minutes} minutes after the shown time?
Starting from the displayed time, what time is {delta_minutes} minutes later?
Shift the shown time forward by {delta_minutes} minutes. What time do you get?
Use a {delta_minutes}-minute offset after the displayed time. What time is it?
Add {delta_minutes} minutes to the shown time. What is the result?
minutes_before: What time was it {delta_minutes} minutes before the shown time?
Starting from the displayed time, what time is {delta_minutes} minutes earlier?
Shift the shown time backward by {delta_minutes} minutes. What time do you get?
Use a {delta_minutes}-minute offset before the displayed time. What time is it?
Subtract {delta_minutes} minutes from the shown time. What is the result?
